title.zh: 卷433 列傳二百二十 金国琛 黄淳熙 吴坤修 康国器 李鹤章弟：昭庆 吴毓兰
title.en: Volume 433 Biographies 220: Jin Guochen, Huang Chunxi, Wu Kunxiu, Kang Guoqi, Li Hezhang younger brother: Zhao Qing, Wu Yulan
title.raw: 卷433 列傳二百二十 金国琛 黄淳熙 吴坤修 康国器 李鹤章弟：昭庆 吴毓兰

translations.literal: Table of contents marker.
translations.idiomatic: Table of contents marker.

sentences.zh: 金國琛，字逸亭，江蘇江陰人。

translations.literal: Jin Guochen, courtesy name Yiting, was a native of Jiangyin in Jiangsu.
translations.idiomatic: Jin Guochen, style name Yiting, came from Jiangyin in Jiangsu Province.

sentences.zh: 咸豐中，以諸生謁羅澤南於江西，使參軍事。

translations.literal: In the Xianfeng period, as a licentiate he called on Luo Zinan in Jiangxi and was assigned to assist in military affairs.
translations.idiomatic: During the Xianfeng reign, while still a licentiate scholar, he sought out Luo Zinan in Jiangxi and was placed on his staff to assist with military affairs.

sentences.zh: 每出戰，部伍嚴整，倉猝犯之，屹然不亂。

translations.literal: Whenever he took the field, his formations were strict and orderly; even when suddenly attacked, they stood firm and did not break.
translations.idiomatic: On every campaign his units held tight formation, and even when struck without warning they stood their ground without falling into disorder.

sentences.zh: 轉戰弋陽、廣信、武昌、黃州，累功擢知縣。

translations.literal: He fought at Yiyang, Guangxin, Wuchang, and Huangzhou, and for cumulative merit was promoted to magistrate.
translations.idiomatic: After fighting across Yiyang, Guangxin, Wuchang, and Huangzhou, he was promoted to magistrate for his accumulated service.

sentences.zh: 七年，李續賓代澤南，使總理營務。

translations.literal: In the seventh year, Li Xubin replaced Zinan and had him supervise camp affairs in general.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh year of the reign, Li Xubin succeeded Luo Zinan and put him in charge of overall camp administration.

sentences.zh: 率師會襲湖口，克之。

translations.literal: He led troops to join in a surprise attack on Hukou and captured it.
translations.idiomatic: He led his forces in a joint assault on Hukou and took the town.

sentences.zh: 進復彭澤小姑洑、泰坪關，擊退援賊，晉秩同知直隸州。

translations.literal: Advancing, he recovered Xiaogufu in Pengze and Taiping Pass, repulsed rebel reinforcements, and was promoted in rank to sub-prefect of Zhili Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Pushing forward, he retook Xiaogufu in Pengze and Taiping Pass, drove off rebel reinforcements, and was promoted to sub-prefect of Zhili Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 八年，從克九江，窺安徽，下太湖、潛山、桐城。

translations.literal: In the eighth year, following the capture of Jiujiang, he turned toward Anhui and took Taihu, Qianshan, and Tongcheng.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth year he took part in the capture of Jiujiang, then turned toward Anhui and seized Taihu, Qianshan, and Tongcheng.

sentences.zh: 續賓戰歿三河，國琛與其弟續宜招集散亡，勞徠撫慰，重申紀律，軍勢復振。

translations.literal: When Xubin died in battle at Sanhe, Guochen and his younger brother Xuyi gathered the scattered and fled, comforted and reassured them, reasserted discipline, and the army's strength revived.
translations.idiomatic: After Li Xubin was killed at Sanhe, Guochen and Xubin's brother Xuyi rallied the scattered troops, soothed and reassured them, restored discipline, and brought the army back to fighting strength.

sentences.zh: 九年秋，石達開犯湖南，圍寶慶。

translations.literal: In the autumn of the ninth year, Shi Dakai invaded Hunan and besieged Baoqing.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth year, autumn, Shi Dakai marched into Hunan and laid siege to Baoqing.

sentences.zh: 國琛從續宜赴援，毀田家渡賊壘，又敗賊賀家坳，斬悍賊胡德孝，賊走廣西，擢知府。

translations.literal: Guochen followed Xuyi to the relief, destroyed the rebel fort at Tianjiadu, then defeated the rebels at Hejia'ao, beheaded the fierce rebel Hu Dexiao, the rebels fled to Guangxi, and he was promoted to prefect.
translations.idiomatic: Guochen marched with Xuyi to relieve the siege, destroyed the rebel fort at Tianjiadu, then routed the rebels at Hejia'ao and killed the fierce rebel leader Hu Dexiao. The rebels fled into Guangxi, and Guochen was promoted to prefect.

sentences.zh: 其冬，胡林翼、曾國籓規皖，精兵猛將萃於潛山、太湖。

translations.literal: That winter, Hu Lin Yisi and Zeng Guofan planned for Anhui, and elite troops and fierce generals gathered at Qianshan and Taihu.
translations.idiomatic: That winter Hu Lin Yisi and Zeng Guofan turned their attention to Anhui, concentrating crack troops and seasoned commanders at Qianshan and Taihu.

sentences.zh: 陳玉成糾眾數十萬，結捻匪龔瞎子圍鮑超於小池驛，救兵迭失利。

translations.literal: Chen Yucheng mustered several hundred thousand men, joined with the Nian bandit Gong Xiazi, and besieged Bao Chao at Xiao Chi Post; relief forces repeatedly suffered defeat.
translations.idiomatic: Chen Yucheng raised several hundred thousand men, allied with the Nian bandit known as Blind Gong, and besieged Bao Chao at Xiao Chi Post, while successive relief columns met with defeat.

sentences.zh: 先是林翼以國琛行軍善規地勢，令率十四營冒雪趨天堂備援。

translations.literal: Earlier Lin Yisi, because Guochen was skilled in assessing terrain on the march, ordered him to lead fourteen battalions through the snow to hurry to Tiantang to stand by for relief.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, knowing that Guochen was adept at reading terrain on campaign, Hu Lin Yisi had ordered him to lead fourteen battalions through the snow to Tiantang to prepare for relief operations.

sentences.zh: 至事急，乃出高橫嶺，屯仰天庵，俯視賊營，皆在目中。

translations.literal: When the situation grew urgent, he came out through Gaoheng Ridge and encamped at Yangtian'an, looking down so that all the rebel camps lay within sight.
translations.idiomatic: When the crisis came to a head, he marched out through Gaoheng Ridge and encamped at Yangtian'an, from which he could look down and see every rebel camp below.

sentences.zh: 賊驟見旗幟，大驚。

translations.literal: The rebels suddenly saw the banners and were greatly alarmed.
translations.idiomatic: The rebels were startled when they suddenly caught sight of his banners.

sentences.zh: 十年正月，賊乘霧登山來犯，國琛揮軍突起躪之，合山下軍奮擊，斬馘逾萬，乘勝克潛山、太湖。

translations.literal: In the first month of the tenth year, the rebels took advantage of fog to climb the mountain and attack; Guochen swung his army up in a sudden charge and trampled them, joined with the forces below in a fierce assault, killed and captured more than ten thousand, and following victory captured Qianshan and Taihu.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of the tenth year the rebels used the fog to climb the heights and attack. Guochen led his troops in a sudden uphill charge, joined with the forces below in a fierce assault, and killed or captured more than ten thousand men. Pressing the advantage, he then took Qianshan and Taihu.

sentences.zh: 林翼疏陳：「非鮑軍之堅忍，不能久持；

translations.literal: Lin Yisi memorialized, saying: "Without the steadfast endurance of Bao's army, they could not have held out long;
translations.idiomatic: Hu Lin Yisi wrote in a memorial: "Without the steadfast endurance of Bao's troops, the position could not have been held for so long;

sentences.zh: 非國琛之出奇制勝，不能轉危為安。

translations.literal: without Guochen's victory through unexpected stratagems, they could not have turned peril into safety.
translations.idiomatic: without Guochen's surprise tactics and decisive victory, danger could not have been turned to safety.

sentences.zh: 」論功，擢道員。

translations.literal: " When merit was assessed, he was promoted to circuit intendant.
translations.idiomatic: " For his merits he was promoted to circuit intendant.

sentences.zh: 十一年，粵匪復犯湖北，國琛馳援武昌，連復孝感、云夢，進攻德安。

translations.literal: In the eleventh year, the Cantonese rebels again invaded Hubei; Guochen hurried to relieve Wuchang, successively recovered Xiaogan and Yunmeng, and advanced to attack De'an.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh year the Taiping rebels again invaded Hubei. Guochen rushed to relieve Wuchang, retook Xiaogan and Yunmeng in succession, and advanced against De'an.

sentences.zh: 賊酋馬融和死斗，卒以長圍克之，加布政使銜。

translations.literal: The rebel chieftain Ma Ronghe fought to the death; in the end the city was taken after a long siege, and he was given the nominal rank of provincial administration commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: The rebel chieftain Ma Ronghe fought to the death, but in the end the city fell after a prolonged siege, and Guochen was granted the nominal rank of provincial administration commissioner.

sentences.zh: 尋授湖北安襄鄖荊道，仍兼治軍。

translations.literal: Soon afterward he was appointed intendant of the An-Xiang-Yun-Jing Circuit in Hubei, while still also commanding troops.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon appointed intendant of the An-Xiang-Yun-Jing Circuit in Hubei, while continuing to command troops as well.

sentences.zh: 樊城地沖要，商賈所集，督軍士筑土城，不煩民力，賴為保障。

translations.literal: Fancheng occupied a strategic position and was a gathering place for merchants; he supervised the soldiers in building an earthen wall without troubling the populace for labor, and it served as a protective stronghold.
translations.idiomatic: Fancheng stood at a strategic crossroads and drew merchants from far and wide. He had his soldiers build an earthen wall without calling on the local populace for labor, and the fortification served as a reliable defense.

sentences.zh: 時捻匪西擾關中，命國琛率師赴援，以鄖西戒嚴，留未行。

translations.literal: At the time Nian bandits were raiding west into Guanzhong, and he was ordered to lead troops to the relief; because Yunxi was placed under martial alert, he remained and did not depart.
translations.idiomatic: When Nian bandits began raiding west into the Guanzhong region, he was ordered to lead troops to their relief, but martial law was declared in Yunxi and he was kept from setting out.

sentences.zh: 同治元年，馬融和以眾六萬圍南陽，國琛越境往援，力戰解城圍，拔出難民數萬。

translations.literal: In the first year of Tongzhi, Ma Ronghe with sixty thousand men besieged Nanyang; Guochen crossed the border to relieve it, fought hard to lift the siege, and rescued tens of thousands of refugees.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of the Tongzhi reign Ma Ronghe besieged Nanyang with sixty thousand men. Guochen crossed into the neighboring province to relieve the city, fought fiercely to break the siege, and rescued tens of thousands of civilians.

sentences.zh: 巡撫嚴樹森忌之，劾其不遵調度，以同知降補。

translations.literal: Governor Yan Shusen envied him and impeached him for failing to obey orders, and he was demoted and reassigned as sub-prefect.
translations.idiomatic: Governor Yan Shusen, jealous of his success, impeached him for disobeying orders, and he was demoted and reassigned at the rank of sub-prefect.

sentences.zh: 二年，曾國籓調統義從營。

translations.literal: In the second year, Zeng Guofan transferred him to command the Yicong Battalion.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year Zeng Guofan transferred him to command the Volunteer Followers Battalion.

sentences.zh: 擊賊徽州，屢捷於豹嶺、佛嶺、黃傋口、小溪。

translations.literal: He attacked rebels in Huizhou and repeatedly won victories at Baoling, Foling, Huangkangkou, and Xiaoxi.
translations.idiomatic: He fought the rebels in Huizhou and won repeated victories at Baoling, Foling, Huangkangkou, and Xiaoxi.

sentences.zh: 皖南肅清，復原官，補甘肅鞏秦階道。

translations.literal: When southern Anhui was pacified, his original rank was restored, and he was appointed to the Gong-Qin-Jie Circuit in Gansu.
translations.idiomatic: After southern Anhui was pacified, his original rank was restored and he was appointed intendant of the Gong-Qin-Jie Circuit in Gansu.

sentences.zh: 以母老假歸。

translations.literal: Because his mother was old, he took leave and returned home.
translations.idiomatic: He took leave to return home because his mother was elderly.

sentences.zh: 光緒元年，起復廣東督糧道，擢按察使。

translations.literal: In the first year of Guangxu, he was recalled and appointed grain transport commissioner of Guangdong, and was promoted to provincial judicial commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of the Guangxu reign he was recalled to office as grain transport commissioner of Guangdong and promoted to provincial judicial commissioner.

sentences.zh: 五年，卒于官。

translations.literal: In the fifth year, he died in office.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year he died in office.

sentences.zh: 國琛以儒生治軍十餘年，堅苦踔厲，號為名將。

translations.literal: Guochen, a Confucian scholar commanding troops for more than ten years, was resolute, arduous, and bold, and was acclaimed as a famous general.
translations.idiomatic: Guochen had led troops for more than a decade despite being a scholar by training; resolute and tireless in hardship, he was acclaimed as a famous general.

sentences.zh: 居官亦有政聲。

translations.literal: In civil office he also had a reputation for good governance.
translations.idiomatic: As a civil official he also earned a reputation for effective administration.

sentences.zh: 黃淳熙，字子春，江西鄱陽人。

translations.literal: Huang Chunxi, courtesy name Zichun, was a native of Poyang in Jiangxi.
translations.idiomatic: Huang Chunxi, style name Zichun, came from Poyang in Jiangxi Province.

sentences.zh: 道光二十七年進士，湖南即用知縣，歷署綏寧、會同。

translations.literal: A jinshi in the twenty-seventh year of Daoguang, he was appointed directly as magistrate in Hunan and successively served as acting magistrate of Suining and Huitong.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the jinshi examination in the twenty-seventh year of the Daoguang reign and was appointed directly as a Hunan magistrate, serving in succession as acting magistrate of Suining and Huitong.

sentences.zh: 剛直為時所忌，引疾閒居。

translations.literal: His upright and blunt character was resented by the times, and he pleaded illness and lived in retirement.
translations.idiomatic: His blunt integrity made him unpopular, and he pleaded illness and withdrew into private life.

sentences.zh: 咸豐三年，巡撫駱秉章廉知其賢，使強起之。

translations.literal: In the third year of Xianfeng, Governor Luo Bingzhang, recognizing his worth through investigation, had him forcibly recalled to service.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of the Xianfeng reign Governor Luo Bingzhang, having learned of his integrity and ability, pressed him to return to office.

sentences.zh: 七年，署湘鄉，有異政。

translations.literal: In the seventh year, he served as acting magistrate of Xiangxiang and achieved outstanding administration.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh year he served as acting magistrate of Xiangxiang and distinguished himself in office.

sentences.zh: 尋丁父憂。

translations.literal: Soon afterward he entered mourning for his father.
translations.idiomatic: He soon entered mourning upon his father's death.

sentences.zh: 鄱陽方陷賊，移家於湘鄉。

translations.literal: Poyang had just fallen to the rebels, so he moved his family to Xiangxiang.
translations.idiomatic: Poyang had just fallen to the rebels, so he moved his family to Xiangxiang.

sentences.zh: 曾國籓方起督浙江軍，辟參軍事，不就。

translations.literal: Zeng Guofan had just risen to command the Zhejiang army and invited him to assist in military affairs, but he did not accept.
translations.idiomatic: Zeng Guofan had just taken command of the Zhejiang campaign and invited him to join his staff, but he declined.

sentences.zh: 九年，石達開犯湖南，秉章檄淳熙募勇千六百人防省城，時出剿賊。

translations.literal: In the ninth year, when Shi Dakai invaded Hunan, Bingzhang ordered Chunxi to raise sixteen hundred braves to defend the provincial capital and sent him out from time to time to suppress rebels.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth year, when Shi Dakai invaded Hunan, Luo Bingzhang ordered Chunxi to raise sixteen hundred militiamen to defend the provincial capital and sent him out repeatedly to suppress rebel bands.

sentences.zh: 達開由寶慶竄踞嶺東，分黨犯江華，淳熙破之於掛勾嶺，遂夜襲嶺東賊營，躡至江、藍，殲殪甚眾。

translations.literal: Dakai fled from Baoqing and seized Lingdong, sending detachments to invade Jianghua; Chunxi defeated them at Guagou Ridge, then made a night attack on the rebel camp at Lingdong, pursued them to Jiang and Lan, and killed a great many.
translations.idiomatic: Shi Dakai broke out from Baoqing and seized Lingdong, then sent detachments against Jianghua. Chunxi routed them at Guagou Ridge, launched a night attack on the rebel camp at Lingdong, pursued the enemy as far as Jiang and Lan, and killed a great many.

sentences.zh: 進剿賊黨賴裕新，乘霧敗之，破杉木根、黃馬寨而還。

translations.literal: Advancing to suppress the rebel band of Lai Yuxin, he took advantage of fog to defeat them, broke Shanmugen and Huangmazhai, and returned.
translations.idiomatic: He advanced against the rebel band led by Lai Yuxin, used the fog to defeat them, stormed Shanmugen and Huangmazhai, and then withdrew.

sentences.zh: 十年，達開黨眾四出，淳熙轉戰於永、道、綏、靖諸州，復宜章、桂陽。

translations.literal: In the tenth year, Dakai's followers spread out in all directions; Chunxi fought across the prefectures of Yong, Dao, Sui, and Jing, and recovered Yizhang and Guiyang.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth year Shi Dakai's followers fanned out in all directions. Chunxi fought across Yong, Dao, Sui, and Jing prefectures and recovered Yizhang and Guiyang.

sentences.zh: 前后三十餘戰，皆捷，累擢知府，以道員記名。

translations.literal: In more than thirty battles before and after, he was victorious in all, was repeatedly promoted to prefect, and was registered by name for appointment as circuit intendant.
translations.idiomatic: In more than thirty engagements he was victorious every time, was repeatedly promoted to prefect, and was registered by name for appointment as circuit intendant.

sentences.zh: 所部曰果毅營，增至三千人。

translations.literal: His command was called the Guoyi Battalion and was increased to three thousand men.
translations.idiomatic: His command, known as the Guoyi Battalion, grew to three thousand men.

sentences.zh: 駱秉章奉命赴四川督師，湘軍名將勁兵多從曾國籓、胡林翼，劉蓉薦淳熙兵精善戰，秉章遂以淳熙與劉岳昭從行。

translations.literal: Luo Bingzhang was ordered to go to Sichuan to supervise the army; many famous Hunan Army generals and crack troops followed Zeng Guofan and Hu Lin Yisi, so Liu Rong recommended Chunxi as having elite troops skilled in battle, and Bingzhang therefore took Chunxi and Liu Yuezhao with him.
translations.idiomatic: When Luo Bingzhang was ordered to Sichuan to take command, most of the Hunan Army's famous generals and crack troops remained with Zeng Guofan and Hu Lin Yisi. Liu Rong recommended Chunxi as commanding elite troops skilled in battle, and Bingzhang accordingly took Chunxi and Liu Yuezhao with him.

sentences.zh: 至荊州，岳昭復留，獨淳熙以所部當軍鋒。

translations.literal: When they reached Jingzhou, Yuezhao was again kept behind, and Chunxi alone led his own troops at the army's spearhead.
translations.idiomatic: At Jingzhou Liu Yuezhao was again held back, and Chunxi alone led his own troops at the army's spearhead.

sentences.zh: 分道溯峽上，次萬縣，聞順慶被圍，率師赴援。

translations.literal: They split forces and went up the gorges, halted at Wanxian, heard that Shunqing was besieged, and he led troops to the relief.
translations.idiomatic: They divided their forces and ascended the gorges, halting at Wanxian. When word came that Shunqing was besieged, Chunxi led his troops to relieve the city.

sentences.zh: 五月，至，賊走定遠，追之，距定遠二十里，望賊屯城西南，連十餘里，城東北江水環繞，賊方造浮橋渡水。

translations.literal: In the fifth month he arrived; the rebels fled to Dingyuan, and he pursued them. Twenty li from Dingyuan he saw the rebel encampment southwest of the city stretching more than ten li; northeast of the city the river wrapped around, and the rebels were building a pontoon bridge to cross the water.
translations.idiomatic: He arrived in the fifth month. The rebels withdrew toward Dingyuan, and he pursued them. Twenty li from Dingyuan he saw their encampment southwest of the city stretching for more than ten li. The river wrapped around the northeast side of the city, and the rebels were building a pontoon bridge to cross it.

sentences.zh: 淳熙分三路進，遇賊即前搏之，擲火焚其屯，賊大亂爭走，二十餘壘悉潰，擒斬數千。

translations.literal: Chunxi advanced in three columns, closed with the rebels wherever he met them, threw fire to burn their camps, the rebels fell into great disorder and fled in competition, more than twenty forts were all routed, and several thousand were captured or killed.
translations.idiomatic: Chunxi advanced in three columns, closed with the rebels wherever he met them, and set fire to their camps. The rebels broke in panic, more than twenty forts collapsed, and several thousand were killed or captured.

sentences.zh: 殲首賊何國樑，解散脅從萬餘人。

translations.literal: He destroyed the chief rebel He Guoliang and disbanded more than ten thousand coerced followers.
translations.idiomatic: He killed the rebel chieftain He Guoliang and released more than ten thousand coerced followers.

sentences.zh: 賊黨彭紹福率眾千餘屯東岸，收集潰賊，竄二郎場，淳熙銳進，欲一戰平之。

translations.literal: The rebel band of Peng Shaofu with more than a thousand men encamped on the east bank, gathering routed rebels, and fled to Erlangchang; Chunxi pressed forward sharply, intending to settle it in one battle.
translations.idiomatic: The rebel Peng Shaofu rallied more than a thousand men on the east bank, gathered the routed rebels, and withdrew to Erlangchang. Chunxi pressed forward aggressively, intending to finish them in a single battle.

sentences.zh: 二郎場在山中，羊腸曲逕，通遂寧兩路，均為涪江阻。

translations.literal: Erlangchang lay in the mountains, with winding goat-path tracks; two routes led to Suining, both blocked by the Fu River.
translations.idiomatic: Erlangchang lay in the mountains along narrow, winding tracks. Two routes led toward Suining, both cut off by the Fu River.

sentences.zh: 別賊硃甲眾數千由青岡壩至，四路設伏。

translations.literal: Another rebel force, the Zhujia band numbering several thousand, came from Qinggangba and set ambushes on four routes.
translations.idiomatic: Another rebel band, the Zhujia force numbering several thousand, came from Qinggangba and laid ambushes along four routes.

sentences.zh: 淳熙遣偵不見賊，五鼓師行，賊燕子窠，擊走之，逼二郎場。

translations.literal: Chunxi sent scouts but saw no rebels; at the fifth watch the army marched, rebels were at Swallow Nest, he attacked and drove them off, and pressed on Erlangchang.
translations.idiomatic: Chunxi sent out scouts but found no rebels. At the fifth watch his army marched out, drove off rebels at Swallow Nest, and pressed on toward Erlangchang.

sentences.zh: 賊分兩路繞山麓上，淳熙知有伏，令諸營左右搜捕，自率中軍策應。

translations.literal: The rebels split into two routes and circled up along the foot of the mountain; Chunxi knew there was an ambush, ordered the battalions to search left and right, and personally led the central army in support.
translations.idiomatic: The rebels split into two columns and circled up along the foot of the mountain. Sensing an ambush, Chunxi ordered his battalions to search the flanks while he personally led the central force in support.

sentences.zh: 兵分，伏賊起，遍布山岡。

translations.literal: When the troops dispersed, ambushing rebels rose and spread over the hill ridges.
translations.idiomatic: As his troops spread out, ambushing rebels sprang up all along the hill ridges.

sentences.zh: 官軍走田塍，泥深輒陷。

translations.literal: The government troops fled along the field embankments, and wherever the mud was deep they sank in.
translations.idiomatic: The government troops fell back along the field embankments, sinking deep into the mud wherever they stepped.

sentences.zh: 淳熙率親卒拒戰，被圍，策馬突陣，陷淖中，棄馬，手刃十餘賊，中矛仆，擁至場，支解燔之。

translations.literal: Chunxi led his personal soldiers to resist, was surrounded, spurred his horse to break the formation, sank into the mire, abandoned his horse, killed more than ten rebels with his own hand, was struck by a spear and fell, was dragged to the field, dismembered, and burned.
translations.idiomatic: Chunxi led his personal guard in a stand, but was surrounded. He spurred his horse to break through the enemy lines, sank into the mire, abandoned his mount, and killed more than ten rebels with his own blade before a spear brought him down. The rebels dragged him to the field, dismembered his body, and burned it.

sentences.zh: 賊懾其軍勇猛，不復追，餘部整隊還，賊亦遁走。

translations.literal: The rebels feared the army's fierceness and did not pursue further; the remaining units re-formed and returned, and the rebels also fled.
translations.idiomatic: Overawed by the army's ferocity, the rebels did not pursue further. The surviving units re-formed and withdrew, and the rebels also fled.

sentences.zh: 淳熙雖戰歿，湘軍之威因之頓振。

translations.literal: Although Chunxi died in battle, the prestige of the Hunan Army was thereby suddenly revived.
translations.idiomatic: Although Chunxi died in battle, the shock of his stand restored the Hunan Army's prestige overnight.

sentences.zh: 詔贈布政使，賜恤，加贈內閣學士，謚忠壯。

translations.literal: An edict posthumously granted him the rank of provincial administration commissioner, awarded mourning favors, additionally granted the rank of Grand Secretariat academician, and gave the posthumous title Zhongzhuang.
translations.idiomatic: An edict posthumously granted him the rank of provincial administration commissioner, awarded state mourning honors, further granted him the rank of Grand Secretariat academician, and gave him the posthumous title Loyal and Valiant.

sentences.zh: 吳坤修，字竹莊，江西新建人。

translations.literal: Wu Kunxiu, courtesy name Zhuzhuang, was a native of Xinjian in Jiangxi.
translations.idiomatic: Wu Kunxiu, style name Zhuzhuang, came from Xinjian in Jiangxi Province.

sentences.zh: 捐納從九，分發湖南。

translations.literal: By purchased appointment he became a ninth-rank subofficial and was assigned to Hunan.
translations.idiomatic: He purchased appointment as a ninth-rank subofficial and was assigned to Hunan.

sentences.zh: 道光二十九年，賑湘陰水災，勤於事。

translations.literal: In the twenty-ninth year of Daoguang, he relieved the flood disaster in Xiangyin and was diligent in the work.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-ninth year of the Daoguang reign he directed flood relief in Xiangyin and proved diligent in the work.

sentences.zh: 從剿李沅發，以府經歷、縣丞補用。

translations.literal: Following the suppression of Li Yuanfa, he was appointed as prefectural registrar and county assistant.
translations.idiomatic: After taking part in the campaign against Li Yuanfa, he was appointed prefectural registrar and county assistant.

sentences.zh: 咸豐二年，粵匪犯長沙，以守城功擢知縣。

translations.literal: In the second year of Xianfeng, when the Cantonese rebels attacked Changsha, he was promoted to magistrate for merit in defending the city.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of the Xianfeng reign, when the Taiping rebels attacked Changsha, he was promoted to magistrate for his service in the city's defense.

sentences.zh: 曾國籓創立水師，坤修司軍械。

translations.literal: When Zeng Guofan established the navy, Kunxiu managed ordnance.
translations.idiomatic: When Zeng Guofan established the river fleet, Kunxiu was put in charge of ordnance.

sentences.zh: 四年，水師攻九江，入鄱陽湖，為賊所阻不得出，令坤修單騎往南康，導往吳城、南昌。

translations.literal: In the fourth year, the navy attacked Jiujiang and entered Poyang Lake but was blocked by rebels and could not get out; he ordered Kunxiu to ride alone to Nankang and guide them to Wucheng and Nanchang.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year the river fleet attacked Jiujiang and entered Poyang Lake, but rebel forces blocked the exit. Zeng Guofan sent Kunxiu alone on horseback to Nankang to guide the fleet to Wucheng and Nanchang.

sentences.zh: 五年，率舟師防瑞豐。

translations.literal: In the fifth year, he led the fleet to guard Ruifeng.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year he led the fleet to guard Ruifeng.

sentences.zh: 以父憂歸。

translations.literal: He returned home upon mourning for his father.
translations.idiomatic: He returned home to observe mourning for his father.

sentences.zh: 既而武昌復陷，坤修從羅澤南援湖北，復咸寧、蒲圻、崇陽、通城，累擢同知，賜花翎。

translations.literal: Soon afterward Wuchang again fell; Kunxiu followed Luo Zinan to relieve Hubei, recovered Xianning, Puqi, Chongyang, and Tongcheng, was repeatedly promoted to sub-prefect, and was granted the peacock feather.
translations.idiomatic: When Wuchang fell again, Kunxiu followed Luo Zinan to relieve Hubei, recovered Xianning, Puqi, Chongyang, and Tongcheng, was repeatedly promoted to sub-prefect, and was awarded the peacock feather.

sentences.zh: 進規武昌。

translations.literal: He advanced to plan for Wuchang.
translations.idiomatic: He then turned to the campaign against Wuchang.

sentences.zh: 六年，江西軍事不利，胡林翼令坤修領新募軍曰彪字營，會湘軍援江西。

translations.literal: In the sixth year, military affairs in Jiangxi went badly; Hu Lin Yisi ordered Kunxiu to lead newly recruited troops called the Biaozi Battalion and join Hunan Army forces in relieving Jiangxi.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year, when the Jiangxi campaign faltered, Hu Lin Yisi ordered Kunxiu to lead newly recruited troops known as the Biaozi Battalion and join the Hunan Army in relieving Jiangxi.

sentences.zh: 復新昌、上高。

translations.literal: He recovered Xinchang and Shanggao.
translations.idiomatic: He recovered Xinchang and Shanggao.

sentences.zh: 由新昌取道羅坊攻奉新，梯城而登，賊死守不能拔，乃先下安義、靖安，后萃軍奉新。

translations.literal: From Xinchang he took the route through Luofang to attack Fengxin, scaled the wall with ladders and mounted the city, but the rebels defended to the death and it could not be taken; he therefore first captured Anyi and Jing'an, then concentrated the army at Fengxin.
translations.idiomatic: From Xinchang he marched by way of Luofang to attack Fengxin, scaling the walls with ladders. The rebels held stubbornly and the city could not be taken, so he first captured Anyi and Jing'an, then concentrated his forces at Fengxin.

sentences.zh: 時江西餉絀，坤修傾家貲，并勸族里富人出銀米餉軍；

translations.literal: At the time Jiangxi's supplies were exhausted; Kunxiu poured out his family wealth and also urged wealthy men in his clan and district to contribute silver and grain to supply the army;
translations.idiomatic: At the time Jiangxi's supplies were exhausted. Kunxiu poured out his family fortune and also persuaded wealthy men in his clan and district to contribute silver and grain to supply the army;

sentences.zh: 又籌銀四萬兩解省垣，收集平江潰勇。

translations.literal: he also raised forty thousand taels of silver and sent it to the provincial capital, and gathered the routed braves of Pingjiang.
translations.idiomatic: he also raised forty thousand taels of silver for the provincial capital and gathered the routed militiamen of Pingjiang.

sentences.zh: 七年春，克奉新，累擢道員。

translations.literal: In the spring of the seventh year, he captured Fengxin and was repeatedly promoted to circuit intendant.
translations.idiomatic: In the spring of the seventh year he captured Fengxin and was repeatedly promoted to circuit intendant.

sentences.zh: 尋授廣東南韶連道，仍留軍，克瑞州。

translations.literal: Soon afterward he was appointed intendant of the Nan-Shao-Lian Circuit in Guangdong but remained with the army and captured Ruizhou.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon appointed intendant of the Nan-Shao-Lian Circuit in Guangdong but remained with the army and captured Ruizhou.

sentences.zh: 是年冬，東鄉師潰，被劾褫職。

translations.literal: That winter the army was routed at Dongxiang, and he was impeached and dismissed from office.
translations.idiomatic: That winter, after the army was routed at Dongxiang, he was impeached and stripped of his post.

sentences.zh: 九年，駐師撫州。

translations.literal: In the ninth year, he stationed troops at Fuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth year he stationed his troops at Fuzhou.

sentences.zh: 江西巡撫耆齡檄督辦撫、建、寧三屬團練，始立團防營，駐貴溪。

translations.literal: Jiangxi Governor Qiling ordered him to supervise militia training in the three districts of Fu, Jian, and Ning, established the Tuanfang Battalion, and stationed it at Guixi.
translations.idiomatic: Jiangxi Governor Qiling ordered him to supervise militia training in Fu, Jian, and Ning districts. He established the Tuanfang Battalion and stationed it at Guixi.

sentences.zh: 移德興，出援徽州。

translations.literal: He moved to Dexing and went out to relieve Huizhou.
translations.idiomatic: He moved to Dexing and marched out to relieve Huizhou.

sentences.zh: 十年，克建德。

translations.literal: In the tenth year, he captured Jiande.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth year he captured Jiande.

sentences.zh: 秋，徽防軍潰，坤修方假歸，其弟修敳攝軍事，守嶺外郭村。

translations.literal: In autumn the Huizhou garrison army was routed; Kunxiu was on leave, and his younger brother Xiuyi took charge of military affairs and defended Guocun outside the pass.
translations.idiomatic: That autumn the Huizhou garrison collapsed. Kunxiu was on leave, and his younger brother Xiuyi took command and held Guocun outside the pass.

sentences.zh: 調回江西，曾國籓令守湖口，而巡撫毓科檄援建昌。

translations.literal: He was transferred back to Jiangxi; Zeng Guofan ordered him to guard Hukou, but Governor Yuke ordered him to relieve Jianchang.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred back to Jiangxi. Zeng Guofan ordered him to guard Hukou, but Governor Yuke ordered him to relieve Jianchang instead.

sentences.zh: 賊由金谿竄東鄉，坤修自撫州迎擊於鄧家埠，大破之。

translations.literal: The rebels fled from Jinxi into Dongxiang; Kunxiu marched from Fuzhou to meet and attack them at Dengjiabu and routed them.
translations.idiomatic: When the rebels broke out from Jinxi into Dongxiang, Kunxiu marched from Fuzhou to intercept them at Dengjiabu and routed them.

sentences.zh: 賊復出貴溪竄安仁，遏之不得渡河，乃竄德興、萬年，將擾景德鎮。

translations.literal: The rebels again came out from Guixi and fled into Anren; he blocked them from crossing the river, so they fled into Dexing and Wannian, intending to raid Jingdezhen.
translations.idiomatic: The rebels broke out again from Guixi toward Anren. He blocked their crossing of the river, so they fled into Dexing and Wannian, intending to raid Jingdezhen.

sentences.zh: 坤修由饒州馳援景德，以固祁門大軍后路。

translations.literal: Kunxiu hurried from Raozhou to relieve Jingde in order to secure the rear of the main army at Qimen.
translations.idiomatic: Kunxiu rushed from Raozhou to relieve Jingde and secure the rear of the main army at Qimen.

sentences.zh: 會賊由建德上犯，國籓令援湖口。

translations.literal: Just then the rebels advanced upward from Jiande, and Guofan ordered him to relieve Hukou.
translations.idiomatic: Just then the rebels advanced from Jiande, and Zeng Guofan ordered him to relieve Hukou.

sentences.zh: 坤修且戰且進，先賊至，城恃以完，加鹽運使銜。

translations.literal: Kunxiu fought as he advanced, reached the city before the rebels, and the city relied on him to remain intact; he was given the nominal rank of salt transport commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: Kunxiu fought his way forward and reached the city before the rebels, saving it from capture. He was granted the nominal rank of salt transport commissioner.

sentences.zh: 同治元年，李秀成自蘇州援江寧，分犯蕪湖，會軍擊卻之，又會克金保圩、高淳、溧水及溧陽、東壩各要隘，遣散降眾數萬。

translations.literal: In the first year of Tongzhi, Li Xiucheng came from Suzhou to relieve Jiangning and sent detachments to invade Wuhu; he joined the army in repulsing them, then jointly captured the key positions of Jinbaowei, Gaochun, Lishui, and Liyang and Dongba, and disbanded tens of thousands of surrendered followers.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of the Tongzhi reign Li Xiucheng marched from Suzhou to relieve Jiangning and sent detachments against Wuhu. Kunxiu joined the allied forces in repulsing them, then helped capture the key positions of Jinbaowei, Gaochun, Lishui, Liyang, and Dongba, and disbanded tens of thousands of surrendered rebels.

sentences.zh: 三年，加布政使銜。

translations.literal: In the third year, he was given the nominal rank of provincial administration commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year he was granted the nominal rank of provincial administration commissioner.

sentences.zh: 江寧克復，以按察使記名。

translations.literal: When Jiangning was recovered, he was registered by name for appointment as provincial judicial commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: After Jiangning was recovered, he was registered by name for appointment as provincial judicial commissioner.

sentences.zh: 四年，署徽寧池太廣道，授安徽按察使。

translations.literal: In the fourth year, he served as acting intendant of the Hui-Ning-Chi-Tai-Guang Circuit and was appointed provincial judicial commissioner of Anhui.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year he served as acting intendant of the Hui-Ning-Chi-Tai-Guang Circuit and was appointed provincial judicial commissioner of Anhui.

sentences.zh: 五年，署布政使。

translations.literal: In the fifth year, he served as acting provincial administration commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year he served as acting provincial administration commissioner.

sentences.zh: 六年，巡撫英翰駐潁州，出境剿捻，坤修轉輸餉運，未嘗遲乏。

translations.literal: In the sixth year, Governor Yinghan was stationed at Yingzhou and went beyond the border to suppress the Nian bandits; Kunxiu transported supplies and never delayed or fell short.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year Governor Yinghan was stationed at Yingzhou and marched beyond the border to suppress the Nian bandits. Kunxiu handled supply transport and never once fell behind or came up short.

sentences.zh: 七年，署巡撫，實授布政使。

translations.literal: In the seventh year, he served as acting governor and was formally appointed provincial administration commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh year he served as acting governor and was formally appointed provincial administration commissioner.

sentences.zh: 東捻平，請假回籍補終父母喪。

translations.literal: When the eastern Nian were pacified, he requested leave to return home and complete mourning for his parents.
translations.idiomatic: After the eastern Nian were pacified, he took leave to return home and complete the mourning period for his parents.

sentences.zh: 九年，回任。

translations.literal: In the ninth year, he returned to his post.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth year he returned to his post.

sentences.zh: 十一年，卒。

translations.literal: In the eleventh year, he died.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh year he died.

sentences.zh: 巡撫英翰疏陳其戰功政績，賜恤，贈內閣學士。

translations.literal: Governor Yinghan memorialized his military achievements and administrative record; mourning favors were granted, and he was posthumously given the rank of Grand Secretariat academician.
translations.idiomatic: Governor Yinghan memorialized his military and administrative achievements. The court granted mourning honors and posthumously awarded him the rank of Grand Secretariat academician.

sentences.zh: 康國器，初名以泰，字交修，廣東南海人。

translations.literal: Kang Guoqi, original name Yitai, courtesy name Jiaoxiu, was a native of Nanhai in Guangdong.
translations.idiomatic: Kang Guoqi, originally named Yitai, style name Jiaoxiu, came from Nanhai in Guangdong Province.

sentences.zh: 少為吏員。

translations.literal: In youth he was a minor clerk.
translations.idiomatic: In his youth he served as a minor clerk.

sentences.zh: 道光末，從軍，以勞授江西贛縣桂源司巡檢。

translations.literal: At the end of the Daoguang reign he joined the army, and for his labors was appointed patrol inspector of Guiyuan Subdistrict in Gan County, Jiangxi.
translations.idiomatic: At the end of the Daoguang reign he joined the army and, for his service, was appointed patrol inspector of Guiyuan Subdistrict in Gan County, Jiangxi.

sentences.zh: 咸豐初，粵匪犯江西，土寇蜂起，國器募死士三百，贛南道周玉衡檄擊賊烏兜、良口，克萬安。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Xianfeng, the Cantonese rebels invaded Jiangxi and local bandits rose everywhere; Guoqi recruited three hundred dare-to-die soldiers, and Gannan Circuit Intendant Zhou Yuheng ordered attacks on the rebels at Wudou and Liangkou, capturing Wan'an.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of the Xianfeng reign the Taiping rebels invaded Jiangxi and local bandits rose everywhere. Guoqi recruited three hundred dare-to-die fighters, and Gannan Circuit Intendant Zhou Yuheng ordered attacks on rebel positions at Wudou and Liangkou, capturing Wan'an.

sentences.zh: 造船三十艘，習水戰。

translations.literal: He built thirty boats and trained in naval warfare.
translations.idiomatic: He built thirty boats and trained his men in river warfare.

sentences.zh: 六年，從克饒州，累擢知縣，署南城。

translations.literal: In the sixth year, following the capture of Raozhou, he was repeatedly promoted to magistrate and served as acting magistrate of Nancheng.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year he took part in the capture of Raozhou, was repeatedly promoted to magistrate, and served as acting magistrate of Nancheng.

sentences.zh: 石達開陷瑞、撫、臨、吉四郡，國器從克樟樹鎮，連戰瑞州、臨江、鉛山、安仁，擢同知。

translations.literal: When Shi Dakai captured the four prefectures of Rui, Fu, Lin, and Ji, Guoqi followed in the capture of Zhangshu Town and fought continuously at Ruizhou, Linjiang, Qianshan, and Anren, and was promoted to sub-prefect.
translations.idiomatic: When Shi Dakai overran the four prefectures of Rui, Fu, Lin, and Ji, Guoqi took part in the capture of Zhangshu Town and fought continuously at Ruizhou, Linjiang, Qianshan, and Anren, earning promotion to sub-prefect.

sentences.zh: 十一年，廣東巡撫耆齡檄剿陽山賊。

translations.literal: In the eleventh year, Guangdong Governor Qiling ordered him to suppress the rebels in Yangshan.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh year Guangdong Governor Qiling ordered him to suppress the rebels in Yangshan.

sentences.zh: 賊踞藍山，地阻絕，負隅十餘年。

translations.literal: The rebels held Lanshan; the terrain was inaccessible, and they had held out in a corner for more than ten years.
translations.idiomatic: The rebels held Lanshan, where the terrain was nearly impassable, and had defied the government there for more than a decade.

sentences.zh: 國器緣崖歷磵出賊后，破石柵九，奪砲臺，毀其老巢。

translations.literal: Guoqi climbed cliffs and crossed streams to get behind the rebels, broke nine stone palisades, seized artillery emplacements, and destroyed their stronghold.
translations.idiomatic: Guoqi climbed cliffs and crossed streams to get behind the rebels, stormed nine stone palisades, seized their artillery emplacements, and destroyed their stronghold.

sentences.zh: 遣子熊飛單騎說降劇賊練四虎，其魁梁柱走豬頭寨，穴山攻獲之。

translations.literal: He sent his son Xiongfei alone on horseback to persuade the fierce rebel Lian Sihu to surrender; the chieftain Liang Zhu fled to Zhutou Stockade, and by tunneling into the mountain they captured him.
translations.idiomatic: He sent his son Xiongfei alone on horseback to persuade the fierce rebel Lian Sihu to surrender. When the chieftain Liang Zhu fled to Zhutou Stockade, Guoqi's forces tunneled into the mountain and captured him.

sentences.zh: 進軍赫巖，擒賊渠周裕等。

translations.literal: Advancing to Heyan, he captured the rebel leaders Zhou Yu and others.
translations.idiomatic: Advancing to Heyan, he captured the rebel leaders Zhou Yu and others.

sentences.zh: 藍山平，擢知府。

translations.literal: When Lanshan was pacified, he was promoted to prefect.
translations.idiomatic: After Lanshan was pacified, he was promoted to prefect.

sentences.zh: 同治元年，援浙，從蔣益澧圍湯溪，明年春，克之，擢道員。

translations.literal: In the first year of Tongzhi, he went to relieve Zhejiang, followed Jiang Yili in besieging Tangxi, and in the spring of the next year captured it and was promoted to circuit intendant.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of the Tongzhi reign he marched to relieve Zhejiang, joined Jiang Yili in besieging Tangxi, and captured the city the following spring, earning promotion to circuit intendant.

sentences.zh: 三年，克餘杭，功最多，授福建延建邵道，始專統一軍。

translations.literal: In the third year, he captured Yuhang with the greatest merit, was appointed intendant of the Yan-Jian-Shao Circuit in Fujian, and for the first time commanded an army of his own.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year he captured Yuhang with the greatest distinction, was appointed intendant of the Yan-Jian-Shao Circuit in Fujian, and for the first time commanded an army of his own.

sentences.zh: 粵匪汪海洋犯閩，陷武平、永平，李世賢踞漳州、龍巖與之合，旁郡縣多沒於賊。

translations.literal: The Cantonese rebel Wang Haiyang invaded Fujian, captured Wuping and Yongping, and Li Shixian held Zhangzhou and Longyan in alliance with him; many neighboring prefectures and counties fell to the rebels.
translations.idiomatic: The Taiping rebel Wang Haiyang invaded Fujian, capturing Wuping and Yongping, while Li Shixian held Zhangzhou and Longyan in alliance with him. Many neighboring prefectures and counties fell to the rebels.

sentences.zh: 左宗棠議三路進兵，國器自請當龍巖。

translations.literal: Zuo Zongtang proposed advancing in three columns, and Guoqi volunteered to take Longyan.
translations.idiomatic: Zuo Zongtang proposed a three-column advance, and Guoqi volunteered to take Longyan himself.

sentences.zh: 進軍雁石，令熊飛壁鐵石洋，三戰薄城下，破其眾數萬，并敗古田援賊。

translations.literal: Advancing to Yanshi, he ordered Xiongfei to fortify Tieshiyang; after three battles he pressed to the city walls, broke their force of tens of thousands, and also defeated the relief rebels from Gutian.
translations.idiomatic: Advancing to Yanshi, he ordered Xiongfei to fortify Tieshiyang. After three battles he pressed to the city walls, routed a rebel force of tens of thousands, and also defeated relief troops from Gutian.

sentences.zh: 四年正月，遂克龍巖。

translations.literal: In the first month of the fourth year, he finally captured Longyan.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of the fourth year he finally captured Longyan.

sentences.zh: 賊走永定，分踞苦竹、奎洋，勢猶熾。

translations.literal: The rebels fled to Yongding and separately held Kuchu and Kuiyang; their power was still fierce.
translations.idiomatic: The rebels fled to Yongding and held Kuchu and Kuiyang separately, and their strength remained formidable.

sentences.zh: 國器進擊苦竹，乘夜大霧，火賊營，破二十餘壘。

translations.literal: Guoqi advanced to attack Kuchu, took advantage of a heavy night fog, set fire to the rebel camps, and broke more than twenty forts.
translations.idiomatic: Guoqi advanced against Kuchu, used a heavy night fog to set fire to the rebel camps, and stormed more than twenty forts.

sentences.zh: 海洋以悍黨來援，敗之於東阬，又敗之大溪，乃竄廣東大浦境。

translations.literal: Haiyang came with fierce followers to relieve them; Guoqi defeated them at Dongkeng and again at Daxi, and they fled into the Dapu region of Guangdong.
translations.idiomatic: Haiyang came with fierce followers to relieve them. Guoqi defeated them at Dongkeng and again at Daxi, and they fled into the Dapu region of Guangdong.

sentences.zh: 未幾，海洋復犯永定，國器馳毀羅灘橋；

translations.literal: Before long Haiyang again invaded Yongding, and Guoqi hurried to destroy the Luotan Bridge;
translations.idiomatic: Before long Haiyang invaded Yongding again, and Guoqi rushed to destroy the Luotan Bridge;

sentences.zh: 賊分七路來撲，海洋自陣獅龍嶺，所部皆死黨，旗幟遍巖谷。

translations.literal: the rebels came in seven columns to attack, Haiyang himself drew up battle at Shilong Ridge, his followers were all die-hard loyalists, and banners filled the cliffs and valleys.
translations.idiomatic: the rebels attacked in seven columns, with Haiyang himself commanding at Shilong Ridge. His followers were all die-hard loyalists, and their banners filled the cliffs and valleys.

sentences.zh: 國器曰：「賊精銳盡萃於此，若摧之，餘眾必奔。

translations.literal: Guoqi said: "The rebels' elite troops are all gathered here; if we break them, the rest will surely flee.
translations.idiomatic: Guoqi said, "The rebels' best troops are all gathered here. If we break them, the rest will surely flee.

sentences.zh: 」乃堅壁深溝，伺怠出擊。

translations.literal: " He therefore strengthened his walls and dug deep trenches, waited for their slackness, and then struck.
translations.idiomatic: " He therefore strengthened his defenses and dug deep trenches, waited for the enemy to slacken, and then struck.

sentences.zh: 先破其伏，分道猛進，斬馘數千，盡獲其軍實，海洋跳而免。

translations.literal: First he broke their ambush, advanced fiercely in separate columns, killed and captured several thousand, seized all their military stores, and Haiyang leaped away and escaped.
translations.idiomatic: First he broke their ambush, then advanced fiercely in separate columns, killing or capturing several thousand and seizing all their military stores. Haiyang leaped away and escaped.

sentences.zh: 時漳州亦下，李世賢西遁，遇國器於塔下，縱兵擊之，降其眾二萬人。

translations.literal: At that time Zhangzhou also fell; Li Shixian fled west, met Guoqi below the pagoda, and Guoqi unleashed his troops to attack him and accepted the surrender of twenty thousand men.
translations.idiomatic: By then Zhangzhou had also fallen. Li Shixian fled west, encountered Guoqi below the pagoda, and Guoqi attacked him and accepted the surrender of twenty thousand men.

sentences.zh: 海洋走廣東，踞鎮平。

translations.literal: Haiyang fled to Guangdong and held Zhenping.
translations.idiomatic: Haiyang fled to Guangdong and seized Zhenping.

sentences.zh: 國器進壁鎮平東南高思塘，分軍扼程官埠，賊數來犯，卻之。

translations.literal: Guoqi advanced and encamped at Gaositang southeast of Zhenping, divided his army to hold Chengguanbu, the rebels came to attack several times, and he repulsed them.
translations.idiomatic: Guoqi advanced and encamped at Gaositang southeast of Zhenping, sent detachments to hold Chengguanbu, and repulsed several rebel attacks.

sentences.zh: 國器知海洋將襲高思而虛攻程官埠，乃戒程官軍勿為動，設伏兩山間。

translations.literal: Guoqi knew Haiyang would strike Gaosi while making a feint against Chengguanbu, so he warned the Chengguan troops not to move and set ambushes between the two mountains.
translations.idiomatic: Guoqi knew Haiyang would strike Gaosi while making a feint against Chengguanbu, so he ordered the Chengguan garrison to hold its position and set ambushes between the two mountains.

sentences.zh: 海洋果率悍黨來撲，誘入，伏突起，槍斃其梟汪大力、黃十四，海洋傷腕，陣斃及墮巖磵死者無數。

translations.literal: Haiyang indeed led fierce followers to attack; they were lured in, the ambush rose, gunfire killed the chieftains Wang Dali and Huang Shisi, Haiyang was wounded in the wrist, and countless were killed in battle or fell from cliffs and streams to their deaths.
translations.idiomatic: Haiyang indeed led fierce followers in an attack. They were lured in, the ambush sprang up, and gunfire killed the chieftains Wang Dali and Huang Shisi. Haiyang was wounded in the wrist, and countless rebels were killed in battle or fell from cliffs and streams to their deaths.

sentences.zh: 胡瞎子攻程官，亦敗走。

translations.literal: Blind Hu attacked Chengguan and was also defeated and fled.
translations.idiomatic: Blind Hu attacked Chengguan and was likewise defeated and driven off.

sentences.zh: 尋克鎮平。

translations.literal: Soon afterward he captured Zhenping.
translations.idiomatic: He soon captured Zhenping.

sentences.zh: 十二月，會諸軍擊賊嘉應，海洋伏誅，餘孽悉平。

translations.literal: In the twelfth month, he joined the allied armies in attacking the rebels at Jiaying; Haiyang was executed by ambush, and the remaining bandits were all pacified.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month he joined the allied armies in attacking the rebels at Jiaying. Haiyang was killed in an ambush, and the remaining rebels were all pacified.

sentences.zh: 五年，擢按察使。

translations.literal: In the fifth year, he was promoted to provincial judicial commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year he was promoted to provincial judicial commissioner.

sentences.zh: 七年，遷廣西布政使。

translations.literal: In the seventh year, he was transferred to provincial administration commissioner of Guangxi.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh year he was transferred to provincial administration commissioner of Guangxi.

sentences.zh: 十年，護理巡撫。

translations.literal: In the tenth year, he served as acting governor.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth year he served as acting governor.

sentences.zh: 十一年，內召，以疾歸。

translations.literal: In the eleventh year, he was summoned to the capital and returned home due to illness.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh year he was summoned to the capital but returned home due to illness.

sentences.zh: 光緒十年，卒。

translations.literal: In the tenth year of Guangxu, he died.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth year of the Guangxu reign he died.

sentences.zh: 左宗棠疏陳戰績，請恤，格於吏議，特詔允之。

translations.literal: Zuo Zongtang memorialized his battle achievements and requested mourning favors; the Board of Civil Office blocked it, but a special edict approved it.
translations.idiomatic: Zuo Zongtang memorialized his battle achievements and requested mourning honors. The Board of Civil Office blocked the request, but a special edict approved it.

sentences.zh: 國器治軍能以少擊眾，常傷足而跛，軍中號康拐子，悍賊皆畏之。

translations.literal: Guoqi in commanding troops could defeat many with few; he was often wounded in the foot and lame, and in the army was called Lame Kang; fierce rebels all feared him.
translations.idiomatic: Guoqi commanded troops with a gift for defeating larger forces with smaller ones. A recurring foot wound left him lame, and in the army he was called Lame Kang; even the fiercest rebels feared him.

sentences.zh: 子熊飛，積功至浙江候補道，勇而有謀，常為軍鋒。

translations.literal: His son Xiongfei, through accumulated merit, reached the rank of expectant circuit intendant in Zhejiang; he was brave and resourceful and often served as the army's spearhead.
translations.idiomatic: His son Xiongfei rose through accumulated merit to expectant circuit intendant in Zhejiang. Brave and resourceful, he often led the army's spearhead.

sentences.zh: 國器數獲奇捷，實資其力云。

translations.literal: Guoqi won many extraordinary victories, and in truth owed much to his strength.
translations.idiomatic: Guoqi won many extraordinary victories, and in truth owed much of his success to his son's strength.

sentences.zh: 李鶴章，字季荃，安徽合肥人，大學士鴻章弟。

translations.literal: Li Hezhang, courtesy name Jiquan, was a native of Hefei in Anhui and the younger brother of Grand Secretary Hongzhang.
translations.idiomatic: Li Hezhang, style name Jiquan, came from Hefei in Anhui Province and was the younger brother of Grand Secretary Li Hongzhang.

sentences.zh: 諸生。

translations.literal: He was a licentiate.
translations.idiomatic: He was a licentiate scholar.

sentences.zh: 從父兄治本籍團練，屢出戰有功，以州同用。

translations.literal: He followed his father and elder brother in organizing local militia in his native place, repeatedly took the field with merit, and was appointed sub-prefect.
translations.idiomatic: He followed his father and elder brother in organizing local militia in his native district, repeatedly took the field with distinction, and was appointed sub-prefect.

sentences.zh: 咸豐十一年，從克菱湖賊壘，復安慶，擢知縣，賜花翎。

translations.literal: In the eleventh year of Xianfeng, he followed in the capture of the rebel fort at Linghu and the recovery of Anqing, was promoted to magistrate, and was granted the peacock feather.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh year of the Xianfeng reign he took part in capturing the rebel fort at Linghu and recovering Anqing, was promoted to magistrate, and was awarded the peacock feather.

sentences.zh: 同治元年，從鴻章援江蘇，常率親兵佐督戰。

translations.literal: In the first year of Tongzhi, he followed Hongzhang to relieve Jiangsu and often led personal troops to assist in directing battle.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of the Tongzhi reign he followed Li Hongzhang to relieve Jiangsu and often led his personal guard in directing the fighting.

sentences.zh: 北新涇、四江口諸役，功皆最。

translations.literal: At Beixinjing, Sikoujiang, and other engagements, his merit was foremost.
translations.idiomatic: At Beixinjing, Sikoujiang, and other engagements, his merit ranked first.

sentences.zh: 又攻枝福山、許浦海口賊壘，招降常熟踞賊錢森仁。

translations.literal: He also attacked the rebel forts at Zhifushan and the Xupu river mouth and persuaded the rebel holding Changshu, Qian Senren, to surrender.
translations.idiomatic: He also attacked the rebel forts at Zhifushan and the Xupu river mouth and persuaded Qian Senren, the rebel holding Changshu, to surrender.

sentences.zh: 鴻章引嫌，奏捷不敘其勞，特旨詢問，命一體議敘，以知州用，加四品銜。

translations.literal: Hongzhang declined on grounds of conflict of interest and in reporting victory did not record his service; a special edict inquired and ordered equal consideration of merit, appointing him as prefect with fourth-rank nominal rank.
translations.idiomatic: Li Hongzhang declined on grounds of nepotism and omitted Hezhang's service from his victory report. A special edict inquired into the matter and ordered that his merits be considered on equal terms; he was appointed prefect with fourth-rank nominal rank.

sentences.zh: 二年，會克太倉，規蘇州。

translations.literal: In the second year, he jointly captured Taicang and planned for Suzhou.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year he took part in capturing Taicang and turned toward Suzhou.

sentences.zh: 分諸軍為兩路，其進昆山一路，以程學啟為總統；

translations.literal: The armies were divided into two routes; the route advancing on Kunshan was commanded by Cheng Xueqi as overall commander;
translations.idiomatic: The armies were divided into two columns; the column advancing on Kunshan was placed under Cheng Xueqi as overall commander;

sentences.zh: 由常熟進江陰者，鶴章督之。

translations.literal: the route advancing from Changshu toward Jiangyin was supervised by Hezhang.
translations.idiomatic: the column advancing from Changshu toward Jiangyin was commanded by Hezhang.

sentences.zh: 迭戰於常熟之王莊，江陰之南漍、北漍、顧山，毀賊壘，破援賊，會克江陰，擢知府。

translations.literal: He fought repeatedly at Wangzhuang in Changshu, Nanjiang, Beijiang, and Gushan in Jiangyin, destroyed rebel forts, broke relief rebels, jointly captured Jiangyin, and was promoted to prefect.
translations.idiomatic: He fought repeatedly at Wangzhuang in Changshu and at Nanjiang, Beijiang, and Gushan in Jiangyin, destroyed rebel forts, routed relief forces, and took part in capturing Jiangyin, earning promotion to prefect.

sentences.zh: 進攻無錫，踞賊黃子隆死守，李秀成屢來援；

translations.literal: Advancing to attack Wuxi, the holding rebel Huang Zilong defended to the death, and Li Xiucheng repeatedly came to relieve him;
translations.idiomatic: Advancing against Wuxi, he found the holding rebel Huang Zilong defending stubbornly while Li Xiucheng repeatedly came to his relief;

sentences.zh: 及蘇州既克，潰賊亦麕聚，鶴章督水陸諸軍力戰克之，以道員記名簡放。

translations.literal: when Suzhou was already captured, routed rebels also gathered; Hezhang commanded land and river forces in fierce battle and captured it, and was registered by name for appointment as circuit intendant.
translations.idiomatic: after Suzhou fell, routed rebels also gathered there. Hezhang commanded land and river forces in fierce fighting and captured the city, and was registered by name for appointment as circuit intendant.

sentences.zh: 詔嘉鶴章：「能與兄同心戮力，為國宣勤。

translations.literal: An edict praised Hezhang: "Able to work in one heart and one effort with his elder brother and exert himself loyally for the state.
translations.idiomatic: An edict praised Hezhang: "You have worked in one heart and one effort with your elder brother and served the state with loyal exertion.

sentences.zh: 此次未行破格之獎，為鴻章功不自私，俾得報勞將士，鼓舞眾心。

translations.literal: On this occasion no extraordinary reward was given, so that Hongzhang's merit would not be selfish and he could reward the labors of officers and soldiers and inspire the hearts of the multitude.
translations.idiomatic: On this occasion no extraordinary reward was granted, so that Li Hongzhang's merit would not appear self-serving and he could reward his officers and soldiers and inspire their morale.

sentences.zh: 指日常州、金陵次第奏捷，克成全功，更當與郭松林、劉銘傳等同膺懋賞。

translations.literal: It is expected that when Changzhou and Jinling report victories in succession and complete the full achievement, he should likewise receive rich rewards together with Guo Songlin, Liu Mingchuan, and others.
translations.idiomatic: When Changzhou and Jinling report victories in succession and the full campaign is completed, you should likewise receive rich rewards together with Guo Songlin, Liu Mingchuan, and the others.

sentences.zh: 」鶴章進趨常州，與劉銘傳會攻，破援賊，解奔牛之圍。

translations.literal: " Hezhang advanced toward Changzhou, joined Liu Mingchuan in attack, broke relief rebels, and lifted the siege of Benniu.
translations.idiomatic: " Hezhang advanced toward Changzhou, joined Liu Mingchuan in the attack, routed relief forces, and lifted the siege of Benniu.

sentences.zh: 三年四月，克常州，賜黃馬褂，授甘肅甘涼道。

translations.literal: In the fourth month of the third year, he captured Changzhou, was granted the yellow riding jacket, and was appointed to the Gan-Liang Circuit in Gansu.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth month of the third year he captured Changzhou, was granted the yellow riding jacket, and was appointed intendant of the Gan-Liang Circuit in Gansu.

sentences.zh: 是年冬，曾國籓調其軍赴湖北。

translations.literal: That winter, Zeng Guofan transferred his army to Hubei.
translations.idiomatic: That winter Zeng Guofan transferred his army to Hubei.

sentences.zh: 四年，以甘肅回亂棘，命赴本任，鶴章以傷發未行。

translations.literal: In the fourth year, because the Muslim rebellion in Gansu was urgent, he was ordered to proceed to his post, but Hezhang's old wounds reopened and he did not go.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year, with the Muslim rebellion in Gansu growing urgent, he was ordered to proceed to his post, but Hezhang's old wounds reopened and he did not go.

sentences.zh: 尋疾甚，國籓為奏請開缺，留襄營務。

translations.literal: Soon his illness grew severe; Guofan memorialized requesting that his post be declared vacant, and he was kept to assist with camp affairs.
translations.idiomatic: His illness soon grew severe. Zeng Guofan memorialized to declare his post vacant and kept him on to assist with camp affairs.

sentences.zh: 未久，乞病歸，遂不出。

translations.literal: Before long he pleaded illness and returned home, and thereafter did not go out.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he pleaded illness and returned home, and never took office again.

sentences.zh: 以捐助山西賑金，加二品銜。

translations.literal: For contributing relief funds to Shanxi, he was given second-rank nominal rank.
translations.idiomatic: For contributing relief funds to Shanxi, he was granted second-rank nominal rank.

sentences.zh: 光緒六年，卒於家。

translations.literal: In the sixth year of Guangxu, he died at home.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year of the Guangxu reign he died at home.

sentences.zh: 曾國荃疏陳：「李鴻章平江蘇，鶴章與程學啟各分統一路。

translations.literal: Zeng Guoquan memorialized: "When Li Hongzhang pacified Jiangsu, Hezhang and Cheng Xueqi each commanded a separate route.
translations.idiomatic: Zeng Guoquan wrote in a memorial: "When Li Hongzhang pacified Jiangsu, Hezhang and Cheng Xueqi each commanded a separate column.

sentences.zh: 請將戰績宣付史館，於立功地建專祠。

translations.literal: I request that their battle achievements be sent to the Historiography Institute and that dedicated shrines be built at the places where they achieved merit.
translations.idiomatic: I request that their battle achievements be sent to the Historiography Institute and that dedicated shrines be built at the places where they earned their merit.

sentences.zh: 」允之。

translations.literal: " This was approved.
translations.idiomatic: " The request was approved.

sentences.zh: 子經羲，官至云貴總督。

translations.literal: His son Jingyi rose to the post of governor-general of Yunnan and Guizhou.
translations.idiomatic: His son Jingyi rose to governor-general of Yunnan and Guizhou.

sentences.zh: 弟昭慶，初從曾國籓軍，淮軍既立，國籓留五營，令昭慶領之，駐防無為、廬江。

translations.literal: His younger brother Zhaoqing at first followed Zeng Guofan's army; after the Huai Army was established, Guofan kept five battalions and had Zhaoqing lead them, stationed to garrison Wuwei and Lujiang.
translations.idiomatic: His younger brother Zhaoqing at first served in Zeng Guofan's army. After the Huai Army was established, Guofan retained five battalions under Zhaoqing's command, stationed at Wuwei and Lujiang.

sentences.zh: 同治元年，從鴻章至上海，解常熟圍，克嘉興、常州，皆在事有功。

translations.literal: In the first year of Tongzhi, he followed Hongzhang to Shanghai, lifted the siege of Changshu, and captured Jiaxing and Changzhou; in all these he had merit in the affair.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of the Tongzhi reign he followed Li Hongzhang to Shanghai, lifted the siege of Changshu, and captured Jiaxing and Changzhou, distinguishing himself in each engagement.

sentences.zh: 四年，國籓督師剿捻匪，昭慶總理營務，統武毅、忠樸等軍。

translations.literal: In the fourth year, Guofan supervised the army in suppressing the Nian bandits; Zhaoqing supervised camp affairs in general and commanded the Wuyi, Zhongpu, and other armies.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year Zeng Guofan took command of the campaign against the Nian bandits. Zhaoqing supervised overall camp administration and commanded the Wuyi, Zhongpu, and other armies.

sentences.zh: 及鴻章代國籓，令赴前敵擊賊，馳逐鄂、皖、東、豫之間，累擢至記名鹽運使。

translations.literal: When Hongzhang replaced Guofan, he was ordered to go to the front to attack rebels and chased them between Hubei, Anhui, Shandong, and Henan, being repeatedly promoted to registered salt transport commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: When Li Hongzhang replaced Zeng Guofan, Zhaoqing was ordered to the front to fight the rebels and pursued them across Hubei, Anhui, Shandong, and Henan, rising in repeated promotions to registered salt transport commissioner.

sentences.zh: 捻匪平，留防江、淮。

translations.literal: When the Nian bandits were pacified, he remained to garrison the Yangzi and Huai regions.
translations.idiomatic: After the Nian bandits were pacified, he remained to garrison the Yangzi and Huai regions.

sentences.zh: 十二年，卒，贈太常寺卿。

translations.literal: In the twelfth year, he died and was posthumously given the rank of Vice Minister of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth year he died and was posthumously granted the rank of Vice Minister of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices.

sentences.zh: 吳毓蘭，安徽合肥人。

translations.literal: Wu Yulan was a native of Hefei in Anhui.
translations.idiomatic: Wu Yulan came from Hefei in Anhui Province.

sentences.zh: 咸豐十年，粵、捻合擾皖北，毓蘭以從九品偕兄毓芬集團練助剿鳳、潁間，從解壽州圍，擢縣丞。

translations.literal: In the tenth year of Xianfeng, the Cantonese and Nian bandits jointly raided northern Anhui; Yulan, as a ninth-rank subofficial together with his elder brother Yufen, gathered militia to assist in suppressing the region between Fengyang and Yingzhou, followed in lifting the siege of Shouzhou, and was promoted to county assistant.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth year of the Xianfeng reign the Taiping and Nian rebels jointly raided northern Anhui. Yulan, a ninth-rank subofficial, joined his elder brother Yufen in raising militia to suppress the region between Fengyang and Yingzhou, took part in lifting the siege of Shouzhou, and was promoted to county assistant.

sentences.zh: 同治元年，李鴻章率師援上海，毓蘭從軍東下，克柘林、奉賢、南匯、川沙、青浦、金山，皆與有功，擢知縣。

translations.literal: In the first year of Tongzhi, Li Hongzhang led troops to relieve Shanghai; Yulan followed the army eastward, captured Zhelin, Fengxian, Nanhui, Chuansha, Qingpu, and Jinshan, all with merit in the affair, and was promoted to magistrate.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of the Tongzhi reign Li Hongzhang led troops to relieve Shanghai. Yulan marched east with the army, took part in capturing Zhelin, Fengxian, Nanhui, Chuansha, Qingpu, and Jinshan, and was promoted to magistrate.

sentences.zh: 二年，克嘉定，解北新涇、四江口之圍，加同知銜，領華字副營。

translations.literal: In the second year, he captured Jiading, lifted the sieges of Beixinjing and Sikoujiang, was given sub-prefect nominal rank, and commanded the Huazi Auxiliary Battalion.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year he captured Jiading, lifted the sieges of Beixinjing and Sikoujiang, was granted sub-prefect nominal rank, and took command of the Huazi Auxiliary Battalion.

sentences.zh: 擊賊吳江八斥、牛尾墩、同里等處，進克平望、黎里，調守嘉善。

translations.literal: He attacked rebels at Bachikou, Niuweidun, and Tongli in Wujiang, advanced to capture Pingwang and Lili, and was transferred to garrison Jiashan.
translations.idiomatic: He fought rebels at Bachikou, Niuweidun, and Tongli in Wujiang, advanced to capture Pingwang and Lili, and was transferred to garrison Jiashan.

sentences.zh: 三年，率所部從總兵程學啟攻嘉興，戰於合歡橋。

translations.literal: In the third year, he led his own troops following Major General Cheng Xueqi to attack Jiaxing and fought at Hehuan Bridge.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year he led his troops under Major General Cheng Xueqi to attack Jiaxing and fought at Hehuan Bridge.

sentences.zh: 毓蘭率槍船冒險渡河，先破賊卡，繞出賊營后，立拔之。

translations.literal: Yulan led gunboats across the river at risk, first broke the rebel checkpoint, circled behind the rebel camp, and immediately captured it.
translations.idiomatic: Yulan led gunboats across the river at great risk, stormed the rebel checkpoint first, circled behind the rebel camp, and captured it at once.

sentences.zh: 進抵城下，賊以巨砲拒河口，學啟被傷，毓蘭率先鋒攻益厲，掘河口架橋濟師，晝夜環攻，轟陷城垣百餘丈。

translations.literal: Advancing to the city walls, the rebels used great cannon to block the river mouth; Xueqi was wounded, Yulan led the vanguard in increasingly fierce attack, dug at the river mouth and built a bridge to ferry troops, besieged day and night, and blasted a breach more than a hundred zhang in the city wall.
translations.idiomatic: Reaching the city walls, they found the rebels blocking the river mouth with heavy cannon. When Xueqi was wounded, Yulan led the vanguard in an even fiercer assault, dug out the river mouth and built a bridge to ferry troops across, and after day-and-night bombardment blasted a breach more than a hundred zhang wide in the city wall.

sentences.zh: 賊死抗不下，賊酋黃文金自湖州來援，力擊走之，遂克嘉興。

translations.literal: The rebels resisted to the death and would not yield; the rebel chieftain Huang Wenjin came from Huzhou to relieve them, but Yulan struck hard and drove him off, and then captured Jiaxing.
translations.idiomatic: The rebels resisted to the death and would not yield. When the rebel chieftain Huang Wenjin came from Huzhou to relieve them, Yulan struck hard and drove him off, and then captured Jiaxing.

sentences.zh: 毓蘭緣梯先登，擢直隸州知州，賜花翎。

translations.literal: Yulan was first to ascend by ladder, was promoted to magistrate of Zhili Prefecture, and was granted the peacock feather.
translations.idiomatic: Yulan was the first to scale the walls by ladder, was promoted to magistrate of Zhili Prefecture, and was awarded the peacock feather.

sentences.zh: 調守溧陽，降賊屯城中，勢岌岌，突有金壇賊至，毓蘭與兄毓芬議乘賊初至破之，設伏以誘。

translations.literal: He was transferred to garrison Liyang; surrendered rebels were encamped in the city and the situation was perilous; suddenly rebels from Jintan arrived, and Yulan discussed with his elder brother Yufen taking advantage of their first arrival to break them and setting an ambush to lure them.
translations.idiomatic: Transferred to garrison Liyang, he found surrendered rebels encamped in the city and the situation perilous. When rebels from Jintan suddenly arrived, Yulan and his elder brother Yufen agreed to strike while the enemy was still fresh and laid an ambush to lure them in.

sentences.zh: 賊敗走烏鴉嶺，毓蘭與毓芬兩路夾擊，擒斬無算。

translations.literal: The rebels were defeated and fled to Wuya Ridge; Yulan and Yufen attacked from two routes in pincer and captured and killed beyond count.
translations.idiomatic: The rebels were defeated and fled to Wuya Ridge, where Yulan and Yufen attacked from two directions and killed or captured beyond count.

sentences.zh: 窮追至建平境，陣斬賊目林得英、黃有才，擒黃金龍。

translations.literal: Pursuing to the border of Jianping, they killed in battle the rebel officers Lin Deying and Huang Youcai and captured Huang Jinlong.
translations.idiomatic: Pursuing them to the border of Jianping, they killed the rebel officers Lin Deying and Huang Youcai in battle and captured Huang Jinlong.

sentences.zh: 溧陽既定，調守長興。

translations.literal: When Liyang was pacified, he was transferred to garrison Changxing.
translations.idiomatic: After Liyang was pacified, he was transferred to garrison Changxing.

sentences.zh: 時大軍已破湖州，毓蘭偵賊將竄泗安鎮，與毓芬夜率健卒八百冒雨疾走，潛渡觀音橋，賊不意兵至，棄糧械而走。

translations.literal: At the time the main army had already captured Huzhou; Yulan learned the rebels would flee to Si'an Town, and with Yufen led eight hundred picked soldiers by night through the rain in rapid march, secretly crossed Guanyin Bridge, and the rebels, not expecting troops to arrive, abandoned grain and weapons and fled.
translations.idiomatic: By then the main army had already taken Huzhou. Learning that the rebels would flee toward Si'an Town, Yulan and Yufen led eight hundred picked men on a forced night march through the rain, secretly crossed Guanyin Bridge, and caught the rebels unprepared, so they abandoned their grain and weapons and fled.

sentences.zh: 追至泗安，降者數千，敘功擢知府。

translations.literal: Pursuing to Si'an, several thousand surrendered, and for merit he was promoted to prefect.
translations.idiomatic: Pursuing them to Si'an, he accepted the surrender of several thousand rebels and was promoted to prefect for his service.

sentences.zh: 四年，調守揚州，移廬州。

translations.literal: In the fourth year, he was transferred to garrison Yangzhou and then moved to Luzhou.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year he was transferred to garrison Yangzhou and then moved to Luzhou.

sentences.zh: 五年，回屯揚州。

translations.literal: In the fifth year, he returned to encamp at Yangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year he returned to encamp at Yangzhou.

sentences.zh: 追論平浙西功，以道員選用。

translations.literal: His merit in pacifying western Zhejiang was assessed retroactively, and he was selected for appointment as circuit intendant.
translations.idiomatic: His merit in pacifying western Zhejiang was assessed retroactively, and he was selected for appointment as circuit intendant.

sentences.zh: 六年，捻匪賴文光敗竄至揚州，為毓蘭所獲，以道員記名簡放。

translations.literal: In the sixth year, the Nian bandit Lai Wenguang, defeated and fleeing, reached Yangzhou and was captured by Yulan; he was registered by name for appointment as circuit intendant.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year the Nian bandit Lai Wenguang, defeated and on the run, reached Yangzhou and was captured by Yulan, who was registered by name for appointment as circuit intendant.

sentences.zh: 七年，尋加布政使銜。

translations.literal: In the seventh year, he was soon given the nominal rank of provincial administration commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh year he was soon granted the nominal rank of provincial administration commissioner.

sentences.zh: 十年，李鴻章調充海防營務處，筦天津機器局。

translations.literal: In the tenth year, Li Hongzhang transferred him to the Coastal Defense Camp Affairs Office and put him in charge of the Tianjin Machine Works.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth year Li Hongzhang transferred him to the Coastal Defense Camp Affairs Office and put him in charge of the Tianjin Machine Works.

sentences.zh: 光緒六年，授天津河間兵備道。

translations.literal: In the sixth year of Guangxu, he was appointed military intendant of Tianjin and Hejian.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year of the Guangxu reign he was appointed military intendant of Tianjin and Hejian.

sentences.zh: 濱海多盜，毓蘭按名捕置諸法。

translations.literal: Along the coast there were many bandits; Yulan arrested them by name and punished them according to law.
translations.idiomatic: Bandits were numerous along the coast, and Yulan tracked them down by name and punished them according to law.

sentences.zh: 修南運河、子牙河堤，及千里堤灣，靜海、軍糧城河道，興水利。

translations.literal: He repaired the dikes of the Southern Grand Canal and the Ziya River, as well as Qianli Dibay, and the waterways of Jinghai and Junliangcheng, promoting water conservancy.
translations.idiomatic: He repaired the dikes of the Southern Grand Canal and the Ziya River, as well as Qianli Dibay and the waterways of Jinghai and Junliangcheng, promoting water conservancy projects.

sentences.zh: 八年，卒，優恤，附祀曾國籓天津專祠，揚州建專祠。

translations.literal: In the eighth year, he died; superior mourning favors were granted, he was given attendant worship at Zeng Guofan's dedicated shrine in Tianjin, and a dedicated shrine was built for him in Yangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth year he died. The court granted superior mourning honors, accorded him attendant worship at Zeng Guofan's dedicated shrine in Tianjin, and built a dedicated shrine for him in Yangzhou.

sentences.zh: 論曰：金國琛為羅、李舊部。

translations.literal: The commentator says: Jin Guochen was an old follower of Luo and Li.
translations.idiomatic: The commentator writes: Jin Guochen was an old follower of Luo Zinan and Li Xubin.

sentences.zh: 黃淳熙后起，獨立一幟，雖非楚籍，并為湘軍名將。

translations.literal: Huang Chunxi rose later and raised a banner of his own; although not a native of Chu, both were famous generals of the Hunan Army.
translations.idiomatic: Huang Chunxi rose later and commanded a force of his own. Though not a native of Hunan, both men were acclaimed as famous generals of the Hunan Army.

sentences.zh: 淳熙戰勝殞身，國琛遭忌鎩羽，皆未盡其才。

translations.literal: Chunxi won battles and died in the field; Guochen suffered envy and had his wings clipped; neither fully realized his talent.
translations.idiomatic: Chunxi won battles and died in the field; Guochen fell victim to jealousy and was cut short in his career. Neither man fully realized his talent.

sentences.zh: 吳坤修、康國器起於令尉，功施爛然。

translations.literal: Wu Kunxiu and Kang Guoqi rose from magistrates and commandants, and their achievements shone brilliantly.
translations.idiomatic: Wu Kunxiu and Kang Guoqi rose from minor local offices, and their achievements shone brilliantly.

sentences.zh: 李鶴章才績出眾，堪膺大用，后竟不出。

translations.literal: Li Hezhang's talent and achievements were outstanding and fit for great employment, yet in the end he never went out.
translations.idiomatic: Li Hezhang's talent and achievements were outstanding and marked him for high office, yet in the end he never returned to public service.

sentences.zh: 吳毓蘭以擒獲巨憝顯名。

translations.literal: Wu Yulan won fame for capturing a great villain.
translations.idiomatic: Wu Yulan won fame for capturing a major rebel leader.

sentences.zh: 功名之際，遭際固難測哉！

translations.literal: At the juncture of merit and fame, one's encounters are indeed hard to foretell!
translations.idiomatic: At the turning point of merit and fame, how unpredictable are the turns of fortune!
